solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Poisonous substance eroded half my ground (12)

indicatorNotes.ground: ground down, as coffee is, so the letters are broken up and reformed

annotation.surface: Someone complains that a toxic chemical has eaten away half of their land.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder runs across three words, and 'half' is just letters here, not an instruction to take half of anything.
annotation.definitionFit: Formaldehyde is a toxic gas, used dissolved in water as a preservative and disinfectant.

entries.clue: He repeatedly claims publicity account is a problem (8)

indicatorNotes.repeatedly: repeatedly means more than once, so the word He is taken twice
indicatorNotes.claims: to claim is to take hold of, so the two HEs hold the middle

annotation.surface: A man who keeps saying that the advertising budget is causing trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'He' does double duty: read once more because of 'repeatedly', the man of the surface supplies both ends of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A headache is a nagging problem, as in 'parking is a real headache here'.

entries.clue: Uncovered notice relating to the ear (4)

indicatorNotes.Uncovered: the covers, the first and last letters, are stripped off

blocks.note: NOTICE without its outer N and E

annotation.surface: A notice that has been left in the open, somehow to do with hearing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' reads as describing the notice; it is the instruction to strip its outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Otic is a technical adjective from the Greek ous, otos (ear), used in medicine for ear drops and the like.

entries.clue: Hot meal is high point when in Channel Islands (6)

indicatorNotes.when in: the high point is placed inside the other letters

blocks.note: a hill is a high point of land

annotation.surface: A spicy dish is the highlight of a holiday on Jersey or Guernsey.
annotation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are Jersey, Guernsey and their neighbours, off the French coast; CI is their abbreviation. HILL sits between C and I.
annotation.definitionFit: Chilli, short for chilli con carne, is a spicy meat stew.

entries.clue: Evangelist spread cheaper religion primarily (8)

indicatorNotes.spread: letters spread about are scattered into a new order
indicatorNotes.primarily: takes the first letter of religion

annotation.surface: A missionary offers faith at a lower price to win converts.
annotation.walkthrough: The R joins the letters of CHEAPER before they are rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Evangelists in the modern sense travel and preach the gospel, so any preacher of that kind fits.

entries.clue: Second means of identifying male animal (4)

blocks.note: a name tag or ear tag identifies

annotation.surface: A second way of telling which animal is the male.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal in the surface, but it is just the unit abbreviation S.
annotation.definitionFit: A stag is the adult male of a deer, the classic example of a male animal with its own name.

entries.clue: Open secret, but not to begin with (5)

indicatorNotes.but not to begin with: the first letter is left out

annotation.surface: Something that is no longer secret, or at least was not at first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Open secret' reads as a phrase, but the split is after 'Open': COVERT loses its C.
annotation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, not hidden.

entries.clue: This woman’s moral principle disheartened dissenter (7)

indicatorNotes.disheartened: the heart, the middle letter, is removed

blocks.note: an ethic is a moral principle; its middle H goes

annotation.surface: A woman's ethics have been worn down by an outsider who disagrees.
annotation.walkthrough: The heart of a five-letter word is its third letter, so only the H of ETHIC goes.
annotation.definitionFit: A heretic dissents from the accepted doctrine.

entries.clue: Censure argument against democratic state (12)

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation, as in Dem for a US Democrat

annotation.surface: Criticism of the case made against a democracy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Argument against' is a noun here, a con as opposed to a pro.
annotation.definitionFit: Censure and condemnation are close synonyms, both meaning formal, strong disapproval.

entries.clue: Doctor claimed for examination she performed (7)

indicatorNotes.Doctor: to doctor something is to tamper with it

annotation.surface: A doctor puts in a claim for a check-up she carried out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the person in the story, but it is a verb telling you to tamper with CLAIMED; 'she' is the doctor of the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A medical is a physical examination by a doctor, as for a job or insurance.

entries.clue: Element of ancient craft close to forgotten (5)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

annotation.surface: A part of some ancient skill that is almost lost.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a skill, but here it is a boat: the Argo.
annotation.definitionFit: Argon is a chemical element, a noble gas.

entries.clue: Tradesman opening regularly for business? (9)

blocks.note: the surface says a trader opening up his shop; literally, a tradesman whose work is opening things
the surface says keeping regular hours; literally, opening is his business, done as routine

annotation.surface: A shopkeeper who keeps regular opening hours.
annotation.walkthrough: The picture is a shop opening at set hours; the LOCKSMITH's business is opening locks and doors for customers who are shut out.
annotation.definitionFit: A locksmith is a tradesman who makes, repairs and opens locks.

entries.clue: Mount last stuffed big cat (8)

indicatorNotes.stuffed: stuffed in the sense of ruined, so the letters are messed up

blocks.note: a lion is a big cat

annotation.surface: The final thing to be mounted is a stuffed lion, as in a taxidermist's display.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mount' and 'stuffed' conjure taxidermy, but a mount is a horse to ride, and 'stuffed' mixes up LAST.
annotation.definitionFit: A mount is a horse for riding, and a stallion is a male horse.

entries.clue: What may help one drive and drink we hear (3)

indicatorNotes.we hear: signals a word that sounds like the answer

annotation.surface: Advice on staying alert at the wheel: a drink will help you drive.
annotation.walkthrough: The drive is a golf shot, not a car journey: the ball is struck off a tee.
annotation.definitionFit: A tee is the peg that holds a golf ball up for the drive.

entries.clue: Former cabinet-maker and roofer (8)

blocks.note: a cabinet is also the group of senior ministers a prime minister picks; 'former' points to a past one
one who roofs with straw or reeds

annotation.surface: Someone who once made furniture and also did roofing.
annotation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher was UK prime minister from 1979 to 1990, and a prime minister makes a cabinet by choosing ministers.
annotation.definitionFit: Margaret Thatcher made cabinets as prime minister, and a thatcher builds roofs of straw.

entries.clue: Period just before she was tempted (3)

blocks.note: the day or evening before a special day, as before Christmas or New Year
tempted by the serpent in Genesis

annotation.surface: The moment just before she gave in to temptation.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is the first woman of Genesis, tempted by the serpent to eat the forbidden fruit.
annotation.definitionFit: The eve is the time just before an event, and Eve was tempted in Eden.

entries.clue: Find out when confident (9)

blocks.note: as in 'as I left' = 'when I left'

annotation.surface: Discover something once you feel sure of it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'When' reads as a conjunction joining two halves of a sentence; here it simply gives AS.
annotation.definitionFit: Ascertain is a formal synonym of find out, with a sense of making sure of the facts.

entries.clue: Who manages to trap island parrot? (6)

annotation.surface: Asking who can catch a parrot on an island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' is a bird in the story, but here it is a person who repeats others, a copier.
annotation.definitionFit: A parrot, figuratively, is someone who copies what others say or do.

entries.clue: Sing awful melody with no hint of musicality (5)

indicatorNotes.awful: an awful version is a mangled one
indicatorNotes.with no hint of: the first letter of musicality is removed

blocks.clueFragment: melody with no hint of musicality

annotation.surface: Someone sings a dreadful tune with no musical sense at all.
annotation.walkthrough: The hint of musicality is its first letter, M, which comes out of MELODY before the rest is rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: To yodel is to sing, switching rapidly between chest voice and falsetto.

entries.clue: Performance involving couple expected on time (4)

blocks.note: due = expected, as in the train is due

annotation.surface: A couple's show that is due to start punctually.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts DUE above T.
annotation.definitionFit: The couple in the clue is the pair a duet is written for, so a two-person piece matches the definition exactly.

entries.clue: Unsavoury character a cop let off (7)

indicatorNotes.off: gone off, like bad food, so the letters are spoiled

annotation.surface: A shady figure whom a police officer let go free.
annotation.walkthrough: Polecat is an old insult for a despicable person, from the animal's foul smell.
annotation.definitionFit: A polecat, figuratively, is a contemptible or unpleasant person.

entries.clue: Line part of suit in delicate fabric (4)

blocks.note: the ace is one card of each suit

annotation.surface: A seam on a suit made of fine fabric.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Suit' suggests clothing, but it is a suit of cards, which includes an ace.
annotation.definitionFit: Lace is a fine, open fabric made in patterns of thread.

entries.clue: Ugly spectacle one witnessed reportedly (7)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: signals that the words are said rather than written

annotation.surface: A person claims to have seen something hideous.
annotation.walkthrough: The sound match relies on a British accent, where 'sore' and 'saw' are said the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A spectacle is something seen, and an eyesore is a sight that offends the eye.

entries.clue: Company adopts radical belief system (5)

indicatorNotes.adopts: to adopt is to take in, so CO takes RED inside

blocks.note: a red is a left-wing radical

annotation.surface: A firm takes on an extreme ideology.
annotation.walkthrough: Red for a left-wing radical comes from the red flag of socialism.
annotation.definitionFit: A credo is a set of beliefs, from the Latin for 'I believe'.
